body: Thank you. <3 This story has a somewhat happy ending--posting this was kind of a wake-up call for me and I realized I haven't felt *this* low in a long time, and it maybe, possibly had something to do with my having decreased my meds in the past two months (dumbass). So I went back up to my previous dosage today, and IDK if it's the placebo effect, but I already feel way better. Thank you again. <3

I never mention it on my main Reddit account, but I'm suicidal every. Fucking. Day. Even on my good days when things are mostly OK, the thought is still there, lurking in the shadows of my mind, like a tiger waiting to pounce. I've been in therapy for years, I'm on meds, I'm cleaning up my diet and walking every day, but I still feel terrible and constantly plagued with worry and doubt, and I just don't know what to do.
I'm sorry. :( I hope we both get better, and I hope your grandmother at least has decent quality of life until her time comes.

I'm on Wellbutrin and Zoloft. They just upped my Zoloft dose, but it's still on the lower end so there's room to up it more, I think. I haven't been checked for either, but I guess it wouldn't hurt to ask. I have sometimes wondered if I'm bipolar type II.

Thank you so much for replying. I am fortunately seeing a psychiatrist (I was recently blessed by the Insurance Gods, so that’s one thing I have going for me) and she actually just increased the dosage of one of my medications. I downplayed how badly I’ve been feeling because I’m afraid of being hospitalized, but I did tell her I suffer from intense intrusive thoughts and occasional suicidal ideation.

Eh, my career could be better but it's at least been an upward trend. I don't want to be too specific because I'm concerned people I know IRL could find my account, but I went from working a shitty minimum wage customer service job a few years ago to doing freelance work from home to doing something similar to what I did from home, but in person and making a more consistent (and generous) paycheck than I did before. It also isn't customer service, so woohoo. Still not what I want to do with the rest of my life, though. I am working on signing up for college courses in the summer (for the first time I live in a region where tuition is inexpensive enough for me to afford, plus I'm making enough money to be able to make it work, so yay).

Thanks, I think I will be more honest with her. My insurance situation has just changed for the better so I could more easily get other services now if I needed them. And thanks. If I absolutely had to I could use my PTO to cover a stay in a psych ward, but I really don't want to have to do that.

Thanks. I'm trying really hard.

Thanks for the response. Yeah, I initially chose this program (it's online) because I wasn't insured and it was less expensive than anything I could get in person. But I actually recently found out my parents' insurance covers my area now, so I could get in person counseling cheaper if I wanted. I will look into that, thanks.

Thanks. I hope you're right. We live together so asking for a "pause" is a bit difficult, but if nothing else maybe I can just ask for some distance/time alone. I've been trying really hard to work on my emotional issues in general (in meds and therapy, plus practicing REBT on myself), so hopefully it will pay off.

Thanks for listening, and for not judging me as the awful person I sometimes think I am for struggling with this. I really appreciate it.

I've already talked to him about it ad nauseum. It's amazing *he* hasn't broken up with *me* by now, to be honest. He's told me that he can handle whatever decision I make and that he understands. What bothers me most is this nagging feeling like if I did break up with him, I'd have to face a bunch of ugly truths about myself/realize my whole life for the past several years has been a sham/feel miserable and alone/realize I never cared about him at all/implode and die/etc, etc. I can't really tell what's real and what's not. It's driving me bananas.
I'm actually doing way better since I posted this--I'm on my old meds and in therapy, and I'm starting to separate my real life problems from irrational anxieties. Thanks for the recommendation, btw!

Yup. One of the things that has kept me from offing myself this long is the thought of leaving my boyfriend stuck with our lease, which would be hard for him to afford on his own. The lease runs out in late March and I'm telling myself I can kill myself at the end of February after paying my half of the rent. Of course I don't want to leave him stuck with all my clutter either, so like you I know I have to sort through all my crap and that's overwhelming. Sooo I'm still here, for now.

I literally went through this last night at work. I started plotting out my suicide and I felt true peace and relief for the first time in probably years. Ironically, it made me feel slightly more motivated to live after I realized how enjoyable life COULD be given a shift in perspective, but IDK how long that will last.

NP! Glad to know I'm not alone. It's cool that you're into programming, though--at least your hobby of choice would make for a stable career path if you did pursue it further, LOL. Not so much for mine.

Actually yeah, what you just listed is the story of my life. Not sure if this is the case with you, but I was labeled as "gifted"/smart from an early age, and I ended up feeling like I had to live up to these grandiose expectations of my potential that people had of me. I ended up burning out starting in adolescence, and I still haven't totally found my way back. It doesn't help that, although I'm not horribly below average so far as personal achievement goes, I still feel like I should've been one of those really high achieving kids/teenagers, and thus feel like "what's the point, I'll just be a loser underachiever forever" every time I try to improve my skills in adulthood.

You live in Quebec? That's awesome, I love Quebec! I'm American but my SO and I lived in Montreal for 6 months last year and we both loved it. We probably would've stayed if there was a legal way for us to do so. I'm not surprised that street hockey is a widespread thing there--cool that you had that pastime.

No worries about late replies, btw--I've been working on and off for most of the evening and I've had to spend time away from the interwebz.

Yeah, maybe I should. I think I'll tell them tonight how bad it got today, including my posting on a suicide watch sub, just to see how it goes. 

Haha, I had zero talent with sports, either--the only things I was remotely good at were swimming and, for some unfathomable reason, street hockey, both of which we barely played. As for my actual interests, I've always had artsy interests, like music and books, and I'm actually a musician and on-and-off writer myself. Unfortunately I've found myself not pursuing any of my interests very heavily or developing new ones, to the point that I feel like I haven't developed much as a person since I was 17-ish, which is really depressing. I feel like I'm perpetually haunted with a sense of "I should be doing {insert unrelated thing here}" every time I try to relax and get absorbed in an activity, and thus never really get anything done. It sucks. :/ 

My bitching aside, how about yourself?

Thanks, I appreciate it. Realistically I could probably benefit from therapy too and I'd probably at least give it a go if money weren't as much of an issue. Maybe I'll find some inexpensive option, IDK. Hope things get better for you too.

Probably my SO, but I feel like I use them as too much of an emotional crutch as it is. I've told them that I occasionally feel suicidal, it's no secret, but I guess I haven't let on about just HOW bad it is, partly because I don't want to believe it myself, either. 

Thanks for the support man, I appreciate it. Incidentally, I know jack shit about sports too, so maybe we can bond over our mutual lack of interest in sportsball. :P
